summary: A registered user can initiate password recovery with a registered email address. The system sends a reset link to that address, accepts a new password of at least 12 characters that differs from the previous password, rejects links after 30 minutes, and blocks further reset attempts after three failed attempts within one hour.

business_rules.rule: A registered user should be able to reset their password using a registered email address.
The system sends a reset link to the email address if it is registered.
A reset link expires after 30 minutes.
The new password must be at least 12 characters long.
The new password must not match the previous password.
After three failed reset attempts within one hour, further attempts are blocked.

scenarios.description: Registered user requests a reset with a registered email address and receives a reset link
User opens a valid reset link and completes the reset with a qualifying new password
scenarios.rationale: Confirms the intended end-to-end recovery outcome

scenarios.description: Reset request uses an email address that is not registered
scenarios.rationale: Ensures the stated registered-email condition is enforced

scenarios.description: User attempts to use a reset link after 30 minutes
scenarios.rationale: Verifies the explicit link lifetime limit

scenarios.description: User uses a reset link immediately before and at the 30-minute expiry boundary
scenarios.rationale: Clarifies behavior at the precise expiration threshold

scenarios.description: User submits a new password shorter than 12 characters
scenarios.rationale: Verifies rejection below the minimum password length

scenarios.description: User submits a new password exactly 12 characters long
scenarios.rationale: Verifies acceptance at the stated minimum length when other rules pass

scenarios.description: User submits a new password that is longer than 12 characters
scenarios.rationale: Confirms the minimum is not incorrectly treated as an exact length

scenarios.description: User submits a new password identical to the previous password
scenarios.rationale: Verifies the explicit password reuse restriction

scenarios.description: User makes three failed reset attempts within one hour and then makes another attempt
scenarios.rationale: Verifies the stated failed-attempt blocking threshold

scenarios.description: User makes fewer than three failed reset attempts within one hour and then makes another attempt
scenarios.rationale: Confirms blocking does not occur before the stated threshold

scenarios.description: User makes failed reset attempts separated by more than one hour
scenarios.rationale: Examines whether failures outside the stated one-hour window are counted together

scenarios.description: Previously issued reset link is used after a newer reset link has been issued for the same account
scenarios.rationale: Covers multiple reset-link state and identifies unspecified token invalidation behavior

scenarios.description: Reset request uses email input with case variation or surrounding whitespace for a registered address
scenarios.rationale: Covers common input representation variations not defined by the requirement

functional: Registered-email reset request and reset-link delivery
Successful password change through a valid reset link
Acceptance of passwords longer than the minimum
Attempt behavior before the failed-attempt block threshold
negative: Reset request for an unregistered email
Attempt after the account is blocked
Use of an expired or otherwise invalid reset link
boundary: Reset link at 30 minutes and after 30 minutes
Second, third, and fourth failed attempts within one hour
Failed-attempt window boundary at one hour
validation: New password differs from previous password
data: Multiple reset links for one account
Failed attempts within versus outside the one-hour window

assumptions: The source requirement's explicit identifier REQ-042 is used as the requirement reference.
A reset attempt includes an attempt to complete password reset; the requirement does not define whether request-stage failures, invalid links, or password validation failures are counted.
The exact behavior at precisely 30 minutes and precisely one hour is not specified and requires product clarification.
The duration for which an account remains blocked after the third failed attempt is not specified.
The requirement does not specify the user-facing messages, whether an unregistered email receives a generic response, or whether reset requests are rate-limited before three failed attempts.
The requirement does not specify whether issuing a newer reset link invalidates older links.
The requirement does not specify password character composition, maximum length, whitespace handling, or confirmation-field behavior.
risks: Ambiguous definitions of a failed reset attempt and the one-hour rolling window can produce inconsistent security behavior.
Unspecified responses for unregistered addresses may create account-enumeration risk.
Unspecified block duration may leave brute-force protection either too weak or unnecessarily disruptive.
Unspecified concurrent and multiple-link behavior may allow an older link to remain usable unexpectedly.
The data category is applicable because account state, token state, and attempt history affect behavior.
